text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/resolved-loader-design-judge.md <<'EOF'
# Cross-judge verdict

Recommend candidate A as the base. It makes the loaded declarations available to existing consumers while correcting the schema constraint that would collapse resolved identities. Graft B's explicit separation of identity assignment from attribution and its typed manifest parsing. Do not adopt B's archival-only destination or C's unchanged name-unique schema.

These scores assess the written designs, not tested implementations. All three candidates produced complete artifacts. There were no dropouts.

| Criterion, scored 1–5 | A | B | C |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Preserves identity and attribution without collapsing distinct identities | 4 | 5 | 1 |
| Imports required metadata and every occurrence safely | 5 | 4 | 3 |
| Makes data useful to current consumers | 5 | 1 | 3 |
| Coherent transactions and retries | 5 | 5 | 3 |
| Appropriate scope and project consistency | 4 | 3 | 3 |
| Total out of 25 | 23 | 18 | 13 |

A earns its lead through its current projection, occurrence identifiers, removal of name uniqueness, and fingerprinted load ledger. It includes raw declaration metadata so declarations with no funding survive. Its transaction handles replacement, concurrent loaders, retry after commit, and retry after later supersession. Its weaknesses are optional wording around attribution persistence, an incomplete display-name fallback for company-only evidence, and a strict freshness policy that needs an explicit default. These are local corrections to a coherent design.

B is the strongest archival model. It retains all observations and decisions, separates identity from reporting selection, and scopes references to a run. Its unique run marker gives a coherent transaction and retry boundary. It leaves the key user outcome unfinished because existing database consumers would not see the imported declarations. It also leaves zero-funding metadata acquisition unresolved. Its added run tables and future serving policy make it a larger task than necessary for this request.

C has useful aggregate and repository boundaries, but the unchanged schema cannot represent distinct identities sharing a display name. Its proposed explicit naming policy is still unresolved, so the advertised projection is not implementable safely as written. It discards attribution basis and unavailable reason from the database. Its usage promises an AlreadyLoaded outcome, while the transaction section promises a conflict error. Atomic refusal is safe but differs from the claimed CLI behavior. Keeping source occurrence IDs only in memory also prevents durable occurrence-level traceability.

# Source checks that affect synthesis

`db/migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql` really does make `funders.funder_name` unique and lacks source occurrence IDs on funding entries. A schema change is necessary to load arbitrary resolved identities faithfully into existing tables.

`exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/identity.rs` constructs two identity namespaces. Statistical and provisional identities include `run-local:{run_key}:{leader}`. Company identities use `source-reported:companies-house:{number}`. B's statement that all identity strings are local to a run is inaccurate. A's unique exact resolution identifier preserves both existing semantics without inventing a new global matching policy.

`exposed/src/lib/domain/models/declaration_resolution/attribution.rs` selects an observation only when it has a normalized name or eligible company number. The identity implementation assigns an identity in both cases. Therefore current valid resolver output cannot select an unresolved observation. A may reject that combination as corrupt output for the supported policy. Keep selected observation and identity as distinct concepts because they mean different things, but a speculative third outcome is unnecessary for the current policy.

The same usable-company path permits selection without a usable name. A's deterministic usable-name rule needs a fallback. Prefer another usable name from the resolved component, then a stable label derived from the explicit captured company identifier. Do not reject an otherwise valid funding occurrence because its identity has no display name.

# Recommended defaults and grafts

1. Load every captured declaration. Reuse raw replay for declaration metadata and verify its agreement with cleaned evidence. Include all consumed raw bytes in the fingerprint.
2. Store only identities referenced by selected payments in the serving funders table. Keep all original resolution artifacts available for full evidence inspection.
3. Persist source occurrence ID, selected observation, attribution basis, selected parent, unavailable reason, and attribution issues with funding entries. These fields preserve the result the user asked to load. Make this part of A's required schema rather than an optional future inspection feature.
4. Adopt B's typed supported manifest contract and complete coverage checks. Preserve published outcomes and validate their references without rerunning statistical resolution or invoking Python.
5. Default to replacing only explicitly included declarations. Never delete declarations merely because a capture omits them. Reject stale captures. Reject equal-time conflicting runs with a clear error until there is evidence for an ordering policy. Exact already-loaded retries remain successful no-ops.
6. Use the exact resolver identity ID as the persistent matching key. Names remain display labels. Choose metadata deterministically from eligible donor evidence and avoid replacing richer existing company evidence with absent fields.
7. Keep one transaction and A's loader lock. Keep run fingerprint and counts in the ledger. Fold schema changes into the baseline pair and verify the live schema before any migration checksum update.

No operator question blocks implementation under these defaults. The main product assumption is that load updates the application's current searchable data. An archival-only interpretation would favor B, but it is a weaker default for this CLI request and the existing application schema.

The implementation should prove distinct same-name identities survive, zero-funding declarations load, unavailable occurrences survive, company-only selected observations load, rollback leaves no partial state, exact retry changes nothing, changed-artifact retry fails, and newer overlap replaces only its included declarations. These are proposed verification cases, not checks already run.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

content.text:
Saved verdict to [/tmp/resolved-loader-design-judge.md](/tmp/resolved-loader-design-judge.md).

Recommended A. Scores were A 23/25, B 18/25, C 13/25. No dropouts.

Two source-backed corrections matter:
- Company identities are globally named; other identities include the run key.
- Valid current attribution cannot select an unresolved identity, but it can select a company with no usable display name. The loader needs a deterministic company-label fallback.

Graft B’s typed provenance and separation of attribution from identity into A. Require occurrence-level attribution persistence and keep A’s serving projection and atomic retry ledger.
